name: Liberal internationalism
summary: Liberal internationalism holds that peace and prosperity are best secured when states, ideally liberal democracies, cooperate through shared institutions, international law and open trade rather than pure power politics. It favours spreading liberal democracy and human rights, collective security, and limited intervention with legitimate authorisation. It says little on domestic economic or social policy, which varies by adherent.
scope: The mainstream Wilsonian and post-1945 tradition: Wilson's Fourteen Points, the League and UN order, and Ikenberry's account of the US-led liberal order, as held by figures such as Clinton, Blair and Obama. Domestic economic and social questions are mostly inferred from the centre-left and centrist profile of these proponents and marked low confidence; it excludes neoconservative unilateralism and realist or retrenchment views.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a foreign-policy question; mainstream liberal internationalists (Clinton, Obama, Blair) sit centre-left, and Ikenberry's order pairs open markets with domestic social concessions.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The doctrine champions open markets internationally but sits within a mixed-economy liberalism, so adherents split on markets versus government.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The doctrine has no tax position and its proponents range from Clinton-style centrism to market liberals.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Silent on corporate regulation; embedded-liberal and market-liberal wings differ.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Liberal values favour civil liberties, yet Clinton, Bush and Obama-era proponents accepted counterterror surveillance; split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Liberal-rights commitments cut both ways; the doctrine does not address it.

state-harmful.rationale: The doctrine builds on states joining institutions and the rule of law; abolishing the state is incompatible.

limit-guns.rationale: Domestic issue the doctrine ignores; adherents split.

empower-police-military.rationale: Supports capable allied militaries and multilateral force, yet no stated view on domestic police; split.

gradual-change.rationale: Expects world politics to shift gradually from anarchy toward institutions and law, and works through existing institutions.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Wikipedia says liberal internationalists hold that multilateral organizations such as the United Nations can limit power politics, moving world politics from anarchy toward common institutions and the rule of law.

free-trade.rationale: Wilson's Fourteen Points call for removing economic barriers and equal trade terms, and later liberal order includes the WTO.

nation-first.rationale: Wikipedia defines the doctrine as cooperating on transnational problems through multilateral organizations rather than through power politics between nations, the reverse of putting national interest first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Wikipedia lists liberal interventions in Bosnia, Kosovo, East Timor and Libya, though adherents stress limited goals and legitimacy.

open-borders.rationale: Favours open trade and exchange but states and their borders remain the units of the order; no eventual open-borders aim.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Names environmental damage as a shared problem requiring international cooperation.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No doctrinal position; adherents split on nuclear energy.

experts-over-public.rationale: Valorises institutions and technocratic multilateral bodies yet is democratic in aim; split.

central-planning.rationale: The order rests on capitalist economic expansion, so central planning is rejected.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not a stated tenet; capitalist markets are assumed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Removal of economic trade barriers is a Wilsonian aim, and liberal internationalists generally oppose protectionism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Favours open capitalist markets; industrial policy not a tenet.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Distributist concern absent from the doctrine.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Capitalist economic expansion is part of the order; abolishing money is incompatible.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not a feature of the doctrine; liberal pluralism favours voluntary bargaining.

one-party-rule.rationale: Promotion of liberal democracy is central, which rules out single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to dynastic-succession: its rationale is about inherited rule, and this statement now asks only about a ceremonial head of state.

reviewHistory.rationale: Liberal democracy is the goal, though constitutional monarchies are accepted; hereditary head of state is not endorsed.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to dynastic-succession: its rationale is about inherited rule, and this statement now asks only about a ceremonial head of state.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

democracy-best.rationale: Wikipedia says the doctrine seeks to promote liberal democracy abroad and holds that relations between democracies are marked by the democratic peace.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as basis of power contradicts liberal democratic institutions.

right-to-secede.rationale: Wilson's association guarantees territorial integrity and independence, favouring stable borders over a general secession right.

natural-rulers.rationale: Doctrine rests on liberal equality and consent, contradicting natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Accepts limited force for humanitarian ends and war, but opposes political terror; adherents split on the absolute claim.

war-builds-character.rationale: Wilson's programme aims at lasting peace and armament reduction; glorifying war contradicts it.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Rule-of-law, liberal-democratic order is secular; scriptural law is opposed.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Built on state participation in public international institutions and law; privatised defence is alien.

military-superiority.rationale: Ikenberry's order assumes a leading liberal power but one that accepts restraints; adherents split on superiority as a goal.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Liberal civic and cosmopolitan outlook rejects ethnic homogeneity as a requirement.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Liberal internationalism sees history as moving toward cooperation and law, not class conflict.

civilizational-union.rationale: Doctrine favours universal institutions open to all states, not unions based on shared civilization.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Individual rights and rule of law are foundational to liberal internationalism.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Order celebrates capitalist growth and its successes; rejects the claim.

restore-past-order.rationale: The outlook is progressive, expecting gradual movement toward a more rule-based world.

direct-action.rationale: Works through institutions and diplomacy rather than direct action.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Opposed to the open-trade order built on specialisation and exchange.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Capitalist rewards and markets are assumed.

production-for-use.rationale: Profit-driven capitalism is assumed within the order.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Capitalism is viewed as productive; the Marxist exploitation claim is rejected.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Directly opposed to liberal democracy and rule of law.

collective-farming.rationale: Capitalist, market-based order rejects mandatory collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Liberal internationalists hold the opposite, that trade and democracy promote peace (democratic peace, Angell).

taxation-theft.rationale: States cooperating through institutions presuppose legitimate public authority and revenue.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individual rights central, but minority and group rights, self-determination of peoples, are also endorsed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Democracy and participation are valued over exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Not a feature; public institutions are valued.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Contradicts liberal universalism and equal rights.

organic-representation.rationale: Representative liberal democracy with parties assumed.

total-state.rationale: Opposes illiberal, unconstrained states; rule-bound order.

national-rebirth.rationale: Cooperative internationalism opposes ultranationalist rebirth programmes.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Point XIV of the Fourteen Points calls for an association of nations giving 'mutual guarantees of political independence and territorial integrity to great and small states alike', which rules out conquest.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal personal rule contradicts the rule of law.

universal-morality.rationale: Universal human rights and shared rules assume universal norms.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not a doctrinal question; adherents split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Return rights for diasporas are not part of the doctrine, and liberal internationalists split between nationality-based and residence-based citizenship norms.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: No doctrinal position; Keynesian and orthodox wings both exist.

economic-freedom.rationale: The order unites capitalist expansion with consent of the governed.

rule-by-example.rationale: Doctrine relies on laws and institutions.

national-self-determination.rationale: Wilson's Fourteen Points endorse autonomous development of peoples, though self-determination was applied unevenly.

force-without-un.rationale: Ikenberry criticises unilateral post-9/11 action as breaking rule-based methods; though intervention in Kosovo bypassed the Security Council, adherents mostly prefer multilateral authorisation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not a doctrinal question; liberal rationalism but religious adherents exist.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Domestic issue; split between centre-left and centrists.

class-collaboration.rationale: Ikenberry notes elites accommodating grievances; cooperation preferred to conflict.

dominated-front.rationale: Opposes bloc confrontation against the West; favours inclusive engagement of all states.

ban-interest.rationale: Capitalist financial order rejects the ban.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Liberal view of states as institutions bound by rules.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim opposed to the doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is a domestic matter the doctrine does not address, and liberal democrats are divided between proportional and majoritarian systems.

national-mission.rationale: Wilsonianism is associated with spreading democracy, yet Slaughter argues Wilson did not seek to spread it directly; adherents split.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Liberal internationalists accept gender equality as a rights principle but have no shared theory of structural patriarchy, so adherents split.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Cooperative institutional order and public health, environmental provision exceed a minimal state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Human rights and liberal equality are foundational.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Whether settler states are colonial projects is a historical-political dispute the doctrine does not engage, and its adherents hold varied views.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Ikenberry's order rests on the consent of the governed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Accepts limited humanitarian intervention and collective force, rejecting an absolute pacifist-libertarian principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Emphasises cooperation over struggle between peoples.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is a domestic labour question outside the doctrine, and its centre-left and centrist adherents are divided on it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rule of law and restraints are emphasised; Ikenberry criticises post-9/11 departures.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Ikenberry notes shared sovereignty and acceptance of constraints through institutions, as in the EU and others.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall votes are a domestic institutional detail the doctrine does not take up, and liberal democrats are divided on them.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Ikenberry's liberal order includes US-led alliances; the US hegemon accepted restraints within them rather than withdrawing.

people-in-arms.rationale: The doctrine relies on professional armies and collective security through alliances and the UN, so replacing the army with an armed citizenry is not endorsed.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification claims are not covered; Wilsonian self-determination favours it, but the stress on settled borders and peaceful change leaves adherents split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: A domestic morality-and-speech question outside the doctrine, on which liberal adherents hold differing views.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The cosmopolitan outlook favours territorial birthright citizenship over descent-based rules, a mild inference as the doctrine is silent on it.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Liberal adherents are divided between religious-freedom accommodation and equal application of general law, and the doctrine does not address it.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Order includes IMF and creditor institutions; but debt relief for poor countries has been backed by some proponents; split.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The order links growth to consent and liberal democracy.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Favours arms control (Point IV armament reduction) and alliance reliance.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Adherents range from classical liberals who see property as a near-absolute right to social liberals who accept social obligations, so they split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A question internal to Marxist debate; liberal internationalism regards the Soviet system as illiberal but has no stated view on its label.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental cooperation is supported, but the doctrine has no stated position on precaution, and adherents split between precaution and cost-benefit approaches.

collective-defense.rationale: Wilson's association guarantees each member's independence and territorial integrity against aggression, as realised in NATO and collective security.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The doctrine is secular but does not call for curbing religious institutions, which liberal rights of association and religion protect; a mild disagreement.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design is not part of the doctrine, and its centre-left and centrist adherents are divided on flat versus progressive rates.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court presumptions are a domestic matter on which the doctrine has no position, and liberal adherents hold varied views.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The territorial-integrity guarantee of Point XIV cuts against such claims, but the Fourteen Points also redraw Italy's and Poland's borders along 'lines of nationality', so the rejection is not absolute.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Equal civic rights in the country of residence fit liberal principles, but the doctrine does not address minority emigration versus homeland-founding, so adherents split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Rejects Marxist historical materialism; ideas, institutions and norms are shaping forces.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The order is rule-bound with institutional constraints; reject court-bound majority claim.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender equality is a liberal aim, but mandatory parity quotas are contested among liberals and not part of the doctrine.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Point III of the Fourteen Points demands 'the removal, so far as possible, of all economic barriers' and equal trade conditions among all nations, the opposite of a closed imperial trading bloc.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foquist revolutionary strategy contradicts the doctrine's preference for institutional change and the rule of law.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The cosmopolitan outlook favours a world-historical curriculum over a nation-centred one, a mild inference as the doctrine is silent on schooling.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Wilsonianism is criticised for accommodating imperial rule, but adherents today emphasise self-determination.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Ikenberry holds the order adapted through concessions.

delink-world-market.rationale: Opposite of the open-trade integration stance.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The doctrine has no theory of aristocratic duty; its welfare and development thinking rests on rights and institutions, so adherents split.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory claim; liberal internationalists generally value free media and would mildly reject it, though the doctrine itself is silent.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian hegemony thesis; Ikenberry does argue that order rests on consent, but liberal adherents do not adopt the ruling-class framing, so a mild disagreement.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Rejects dependency theory; trade is positive-sum.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The doctrine does not address constitutional founding values, and adherents split between anti-fascist and neutral constitutionalism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Liberal internationalists often condemn both fascism and communism as illiberal, but the doctrine does not address equivalence, and adherents differ.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Universal liberal democratic norms; promotes democracy globally.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Civilian control of the military is part of liberal-democratic constitutionalism, which the doctrine promotes, so adherents reject a political guardian role.

paid-care-work.rationale: A domestic labour-policy issue the doctrine does not address, with adherents divided.

office-by-exam.rationale: Examination-based civil services are accepted by liberals, but the doctrine has no view on replacing election or patronage by exam, so adherents split.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is a domestic question the doctrine does not address, and centre-left and market-liberal adherents differ.

single-official-language.rationale: The pluralist, cooperative outlook leans against forcing one language on a state, a mild inference as the doctrine is silent.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The order celebrates capitalist growth and consumption, but the doctrine has no view on consumerism itself, so adherents split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Rule-based methods preferred; Libya-style support was debated.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Wilson's proposed league exists to guarantee the political independence of small states as well as great ones, so a great power occupying an ally to hold it in its bloc breaks the core guarantee.

democratic-peace.rationale: The democratic peace thesis is a core liberal-internationalist claim and justifies the focus on democracy promotion.

non-intervention.rationale: Liberal internationalism accepts limited intervention with legitimate authorisation, for example to stop atrocities or protect human rights, so an absolute ban on intervention is rejected.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The tradition is built on human rights, equality and open, pluralist liberal democracy, so conspiracy claims against minorities are rejected.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Wilson's first point calls for open covenants openly arrived at and the liberal order stresses transparency and accountable government, though national-security secrecy is accepted.

local-production.rationale: Wilson's Fourteen Points call for removing economic barriers and equalising trade conditions, and the liberal order is built on open trade, so a norm of local production runs against it.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The tradition favours international law, a general association of nations and institutional limits on even the hegemon, so national law is not placed above them.

religious-nation.rationale: The tradition favours liberal democracy, human rights and self-determination of peoples on civic terms, which do not make religion a condition of belonging.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Liberal internationalism favours sovereign equality of states under common rules and rejects tributary hierarchy; Wilson's Fourteen Points call for open diplomacy and equal guarantees for great and small states.

defeat-communism.rationale: Liberal internationalism, from Wilson on, sought the defeat or containment of authoritarian rivals including communism during the Cold War, though it also backed arms control and engagement (s1, s4).

majority-settlement.rationale: Liberal internationalism rejects ethnic nationalism and state engineering of ethnic composition, and favours self-determination and minority rights (s2).

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Liberal internationalists treat capitalist open markets and democracy as the sound basis and do not seek a third way (s3).

suppress-opposition.rationale: The doctrine seeks to spread liberal democracy, which requires free opposition and independent organisations.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Wilson's Fourteen Points call for colonial claims to weigh the interests of the populations concerned equally, and the doctrine is built on self-determination.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The doctrine centres on representative liberal democracy and institutions and does not take a line on direct workplace participation; adherents vary.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not a foreign-policy question; centre-left adherents are sympathetic but centrists are not, so adherents are split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The doctrine is centrist and cross-party in character but does not claim left and right are obsolete; adherents are split.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The order rests on the consent of the governed rather than any divine source, so authority comes from the people.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Collective security through a general association of nations and alliances runs against standing aloof from blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Liberal democracy is the goal, though constitutional monarchies are accepted; hereditary head of state is not endorsed. (Moved from monarchy-legitimate, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about ceremonial heads of state.)

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule of law at home and abroad underpins the liberal order: Wilson sought international law and Ikenberry stresses rules and institutional limits on power.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Domestic economic policy varies by adherent; the doctrine is silent.

municipal-property.rationale: Adherents favour open markets and private ownership, with no role for local community ownership of production.

family-wage.rationale: Domestic wage policy varies by adherent.

person-over-state.rationale: Human rights and individual liberty are central to liberal internationalism, whose Kantian roots hold persons as ends.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Liberal internationalism accepts collective-security action and limited authorised intervention beyond defence, such as under UN authority.

free-public-college.rationale: Domestic education finance is outside the doctrine and centre-left and centrist adherents split between free tuition and fee-based public colleges.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The doctrine is silent on this and adherents split between equal-rights liberal feminism and views that women bring distinct values.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Wilson's Point I demands open covenants of peace openly arrived at, with diplomacy proceeding frankly and in the public view.

capital-controls.rationale: Liberal internationalism pairs institutions with open trade and an open economic order, so state control of capital movements runs against it, though the order's own texts focus mainly on trade.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Wilson's collective security rests on states fighting aggressors under lawful orders, so refusal is not endorsed.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Adherents split between deficit-averse centrists and stimulus-minded liberals; no doctrine on it.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Ikenberry's liberal order is defended as broadly fair and in need of renewal rather than overturning, so adherents prefer reform within it.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The tradition works through existing states and institutions and rejects revolutionary methods.

sacred-nation.rationale: The tradition places international law and community above national loyalty and treats the nation as a political arrangement.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Universal human rights are central to the tradition; fixed human nature is an inference from them.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not a foreign-policy question; the order pairs open trade with domestic concessions, but farm policy is left to adherents.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Promoting human rights and liberal democracy includes equal property rights for women; not specifically stated.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Mainstream centre-left adherents favour regulatory agencies over private suits; the doctrine is silent.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Liberal internationalism stresses international law and accountability for aggression and atrocities, which makes international tribunals a natural instrument of the rules-based order.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Wilson's Fourteen Points called for autonomous development of the nationalities of the Ottoman and Austro-Hungarian empires, an early statement of minority self-rule.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Wilson's principle of self-determination, with territorial questions settled in the interests of the populations concerned, supports letting inhabitants decide.

simple-living.rationale: The doctrine is indifferent to personal lifestyle; adherents are mostly pro-trade and not asceticism advocates, but it takes no stand.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Human rights and international law are central to the tradition, which rules out state killing without trial.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Domestic tax policy varies by adherent, as the profile notes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Domestic social policy varies by adherent, as the profile notes.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not a foreign-policy question; Ikenberry's order pairs open markets with social concessions, but adherents differ over taxes on finance.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The doctrine stresses international law and legitimacy, but does not take a position on natural-law claims about unjust law.

multipolar-world.rationale: Wilson's general association of nations and Ikenberry's liberal order favour a rules-based order led by liberal democracies, with the US hegemon accepting institutional limits, not several independent power centres.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Liberal internationalism rests on liberal and market-capitalist premises, including the open trade of the Fourteen Points, and has no place for the Marxist labour theory of value.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Liberal internationalism promotes liberal democracy and capitalist expansion and rejects single-party rule.

missingStatements.text: Democracies rarely go to war with one another, so spreading democracy makes the world more peaceful.
missingStatements.rationale: The democratic peace thesis is a core liberal-internationalist claim and justifies the focus on democracy promotion.

missingStatements.text: Peace is best secured by a standing association of nations whose rules bind all members, great powers included.
missingStatements.rationale: Wilson's Point XIV and later UN-centred multilateralism make a permanent general association of nations the doctrine's signature institution.

missingStatements.text: A dominant power should accept limits on its own freedom of action through international rules and institutions.
missingStatements.rationale: Ikenberry's account stresses that the US hegemon accepted institutional restraints, giving the order legitimacy through consent.

notes: Neoconservative and humanitarian-hawk strands would endorse force without UN approval and national mission more strongly; the institutionalist strand would reject both. Domestic positions vary widely.
